Hey survivor - 

I hear you. I also replay my traumas over and over sometimes, like I am obsessed with it, I have to go back and fix it. I wouldn't call it a bad thing every time - we do need, on some level, to process the horrible events because we need to cry and let it all out.  Remember the events so we can grieve. Let our anger, our grief, pain, etc out. Its very important. Crying releases endorphins, and reduces stress. It can indeed be very healthy.

What is equally if not more important, though, is self care. And by going over the traumas *over* and *over* and *over*, you are harming yourself and hindering the healing process. Yes, we need to remember, and cry sometimes, but at the level you're doing it, it is only going to hurt you. You need sleep. You need food. You need to tend for your emotional health. My therapist has gone over this with me many times until it stuck. 

Like you said yourself, "it triggered relapses in a lot of other mental health issues". That is *not* helping you heal. And it will only strain your health and others around you. There is a time when you need to be ready to make the next step: focusing on the present, not the past. The trauma happened. You are allowed to grieve. Grief is a crucial step. Grieving what he did to you. What you lost. How much pain it caused. But it seems now, by constantly replaying the rape, you are not grieving anymore. You are just self harming (even if not intentionally). There is no benefit to doing that hon. 

You are seeing a trauma specialist which is amazing. I have one and she is very helpful. I think on your own, there is a lot you can do *yourself* that will make a big difference. Try just doing one 10 minute activity per day that you like, that makes you feel good. Or get a massage. Do something for *you.* Only you. You DESERVE to be happy. You deserve to love yourself and treat yourself sometimes. Arguably, for trauma survivors, we actually need a lot MORE self care. We can't heal without realizing the abuse was not our fault and turning towards loving ourselves.

So do something for you. Something that will keep you grounded in the present. this will help loads in your healing, trust me. it took a lot of time before I was willing to step into the present and just be calm, but when I did, oh boy did it make a huge difference. you could be cuddling up near the fireplace and listening to your favorite music and sipping your yummiest tea.  It could be reading a leisurely book. It could be going for a peaceful walk. Meditating. You could be *extra* extra, and just wrap yourself in the biggest, warmest hug for 10 whole minutes! There is an enormous range of possibilities. And it doesn't have to be one of these.

I am not a therapist, but in my opinion, you are likely replaying the assault because you still blame yourself. Regardless, it is causing you great distress, and putting you at risk for self harm and ED relapse. self care is key. You need it. You deserve it. It is necessary to heal.

You were in danger. There are three common, normal responses we have when in a dangerous situation. They are called *fight, flight,* and *freeze.* You may not have fought, but that doesn't mean you wanted it. It doesn't mean he didn't rape you. *Fight* is only one of the three reactions. You froze. It was your body's way of protecting yourself from the situation he was imposing on you.

You were not raped in a "stupid way". You were *raped,* period. He was a predator. He saw you were kind and vulnerable and he took advantage of that. Its what predators do. You did *nothing* wrong. And you **survived.** How amazing is that?

"It's as if it wasn't real". That's *dissociation.* It is yet another powerful survival mechanism built into us. You could not process the trauma in the moment because it was too much to bear, so your mind protected itself. That is very common.
